extracted.intended_audience: national banks, federal savings associations, FDIC-supervised institutions, federally insured credit unions, compliance officers, legal counsel, and other regulated stakeholders and public commenters
extracted.subtask_short: AML/CFT program requirements for banks/credit unions
extracted.subtask_description: A Federal Register proposed rule establishing anti-money laundering/countering the financing of terrorism (AML/CFT) program requirements, supervisory procedures, consultation and information‑sharing rules, and related administrative analyses for national banks, savings associations, FDIC‑supervised institutions, and federally insured credit unions. The page also solicits public comments on PRA burdens, plain language, and regulatory impact matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork Reduction Act (PRA) — OMB control requirement and NCUA information collection
rubrics_metrics.description: No agency may conduct or sponsor, nor is the respondent required to respond to, an information collection unless it displays a currently valid OMB control number. The OCC and FDIC determined the proposed rule does not create any information collection. The NCUA proposes to extend for three years, with revision, its information collection (Title: Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism Program Requirements; OMB Control Number: 3133-0108).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NCUA provides an estimated annual burden table (total estimated annual burden: 80,856 hours) showing respondents, responses per respondent, average time per response, and totals for establishing and maintaining AML/CFT programs. The NCUA invites comments on PRA issues and instructs commenters to send written comments within 30 days to www.reginfo.gov (find under 'Currently under 30‑day Review—Open for Public Comments').

rubrics_metrics.name: PRA — Requests for public comment (questions a–e)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Agencies invite comments on: (a) whether the collections of information are necessary for the proper performance of the Agencies' functions, including practical utility; (b) the accuracy of the Agencies' burden estimates, including methodology and assumptions; (c) ways to enhance the quality, utility, and clarity of the information to be collected; (d) ways to minimize the burden of the collections, including automated techniques; and (e) estimates of capital/start‑up and operating costs to provide information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments on reporting/recordkeeping/disclosure requirements and burden estimates should be sent to addresses in the ADDRESSES section and to reginfo.gov; the NCUA summary includes the burden table and instructions for locating the docket.

rubrics_metrics.name: Riegle Community Development and Regulatory Improvement Act (RCDRIA) considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: In determining effective date and administrative compliance requirements for new regulations that impose additional reporting/disclosure/other requirements on IDIs, agencies must consider administrative burdens on depository institutions (including small institutions) and customers, consistent with safety and soundness and the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 302(b) requires that new regulations imposing additional requirements take effect on the first day of a calendar quarter that begins on or after the publication date in final form. The Agencies invite comments to inform their consideration of RCDRIA obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain Language requirement and invitation for comment
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 722 of the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act requires the Federal banking Agencies to use plain language in proposed and final rulemakings published in the Federal Register after January 1, 2000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Agencies ask commenters: Have the Agencies organized the material to suit your needs? Are requirements clearly stated? Does the rule contain unclear jargon? Would a different format (grouping, headings, paragraphing) improve clarity? What else could the Agencies do to make the proposed rule easier to understand?

rubrics_metrics.name: Providing Accountability Through Transparency Act requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A notice of proposed rulemaking must include the internet address of a plain‑language summary of the proposed rule of not more than 100 words, posted on the Agencies' websites per the E‑Government Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposal and the required summary can be found on regulations.gov by searching relevant docket IDs and on the Agencies' websites; the docket IDs are provided (e.g., OCC-2024-0005, NCUA-2024-0033).

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Order 12866/13563 cost‑benefit assessment requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Executive Order 12866 (as affirmed and supplemented by EO 13563) directs agencies to assess costs and benefits of available regulatory alternatives and, if regulation is necessary, select approaches that maximize net benefits. OIRA has determined this rulemaking is an 'economically significant regulatory action.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The draft rule was submitted to OIRA for review. Agencies have assessed costs and benefits and made a reasoned determination that benefits justify costs. If finalized as proposed, the rule is not expected to be a regulatory action under EO 14192 because it imposes no more than de minimis costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unfunded Mandates Reform Act (UMRA) threshold analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Under UMRA, agencies must analyze whether a proposed rule includes a Federal mandate that may result in expenditures of $100 million or more in any one year (adjusted dollar figure stated; $187 million as adjusted). If the UMRA threshold is met, a written statement (including a cost‑benefit analysis) is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The OCC estimates the proposed rule would not require additional expenditures beyond those required by FinCEN's concurrently issued proposal and thus would not meet the UMRA threshold; UMRA does not apply to regulations that incorporate statutory requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Order 13132 (Federalism) consideration (NCUA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should consider effects on State and local interests and distribution of power among levels of government. NCUA expects minor effects and notes the proposed rule applies to all federally insured credit unions including State‑chartered credit unions, as set by statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NCUA works cooperatively with State regulators and welcomes comments on ways to eliminate or minimize potential Federalism impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of effects on families (T&GG Appropriations Act sec. 654) (NCUA)
rubrics_metrics.description: NCUA has determined the proposed rule would not affect family well‑being within the meaning of the relevant statute; any effect is expected to be indirect because the rule concerns credit unions' AML/CFT programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: OCC/FDIC quantitative 'burdensome' threshold used in burden analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: The OCC and FDIC present analysis using a threshold for 'burdensome' compliance as a compliance cost exceeding 5 percent of compensation expense or 2.5 percent of total non‑interest expense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NCUA notes these thresholds may not directly carry over to credit unions due to structural differences (cooperative status, compensation expense per employee, volunteer support) and suggests materiality thresholds for credit unions may be higher.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — AML/CFT enforcement action
rubrics_metrics.description: An AML/CFT enforcement action means any formal or informal action taken by the agency (OCC/FDIC/NCUA) under authority of 12 U.S.C. 1818 (or agency statute) or other applicable law that seeks to penalize, remedy, prevent, or respond to noncompliance with past or ongoing violations or deficiencies relating to an AML/CFT requirement; includes cease‑and‑desist orders, written agreements, consent orders, memoranda of understanding, or assessment of civil money penalties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definition appears in each agency's proposed subpart and frames what enforcement responses the agency may take.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — AML/CFT requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: AML/CFT requirement means (i) a requirement of the Bank Secrecy Act or implementing regulations at 31 CFR chapter X; or (ii) a requirement prescribed under the agency's statutory authority (e.g., 12 U.S.C. 1818(s), 1786(q)) or the section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Significant AML/CFT supervisory action
rubrics_metrics.description: A significant AML/CFT supervisory action means any written communication or other formal supervisory determination that (i) identifies one or more alleged deficiencies, weaknesses, violations of law, or unsafe or unsound practices/conditions relating to an AML/CFT requirement; (ii) communicates supervisory expectations regarding remedial measures required to correct the deficiency; and (iii) contemplates significant or programmatic actions or remedial measures to be taken by the supervised institution. Does not include examiner observations, suggestions, or other informal comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definition sets the threshold for what supervisory communications rise to a 'significant' level and therefore triggers consultation/notice and other procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: General requirement — establish and maintain an effective AML/CFT program
rubrics_metrics.description: Each national bank, Federal savings association, FDIC‑supervised institution, and credit union must establish and maintain an effective AML/CFT program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance is achieved by establishing the program per the establishment paragraph and maintaining it by implementing the program per the implementation paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: AML/CFT program establishment — risk‑based internal policies, procedures, and controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions must establish a risk‑based set of internal policies, procedures, and controls reasonably designed to ensure compliance with the Bank Secrecy Act and implementing regulations at 31 CFR chapter X, including requirements to identify, assess, and document money laundering, terrorist financing, and other illicit finance risks through risk assessment processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Risk assessment processes must: (A) evaluate risks of business activities (products, services, distribution channels, customers, geographic locations); (B) review and, as appropriate, incorporate AML/CFT priorities (31 CFR 1010.100); and (C) be updated promptly upon any change the institution knows or has reason to know significantly changes its risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk mitigation — direct resources toward higher‑risk customers/activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions must mitigate money‑laundering, terrorist‑financing, and other illicit finance risks consistent with their risk assessment processes, including by directing more attention and resources toward higher‑risk customers and activities, consistent with the institution's risk profile, rather than toward lower‑risk customers and activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ongoing customer due diligence (CDD)
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions must conduct ongoing customer due diligence to: (A) understand the nature and purpose of customer relationships for developing a customer risk profile; and (B) conduct ongoing monitoring to identify and report suspicious transactions and, on a risk basis, to maintain and update customer information (including information regarding beneficial owners of legal entity customers as defined in 31 CFR 1010.230).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement emphasizes both profile creation and risk‑based ongoing monitoring and record maintenance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent AML/CFT program testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions must establish independent AML/CFT program testing to be conducted by institution personnel or by an outside party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The testing must be independent (i.e., not performed by the personnel responsible for day‑to‑day compliance) and is a required element of the program establishment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of an AML/CFT program responsible individual
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions must designate an individual who is (i) located in the United States; (ii) accessible to, and subject to oversight and supervision by, FinCEN and the applicable banking agency; and (iii) responsible for establishing and implementing the AML/CFT program and coordinating and monitoring day‑to‑day compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This establishes single‑point accountability and requires the individual to be reachable by regulators and located in the U.S.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ongoing employee training program
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions must establish an ongoing employee training program as part of their AML/CFT program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training is required to ensure personnel understand obligations and can implement program elements; it must be ongoing (not one‑time).

rubrics_metrics.name: AML/CFT program implementation — 'in all material respects'
rubrics_metrics.description: An institution implements an AML/CFT program if it implements, in all material respects, the program required under the establishment paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ties compliance to substantive, material implementation rather than only having written documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written AML/CFT program and approval by governing body
rubrics_metrics.description: An institution's AML/CFT program must be written and must be approved by the institution's board of directors, an equivalent governing body, or appropriate senior management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requires formal, board‑level governance/acknowledgment of the program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Customer identification program (CIP) requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each institution shall implement a customer identification program in accordance with 31 CFR 1020.220 (or applicable CIP regulation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This cross‑references existing CIP regulatory requirements rather than restating them in full.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement and supervision policy — general safe harbor and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Except with respect to a significant or systemic failure to implement the AML/CFT program in accordance with implementation requirements, an institution that has established an AML/CFT program in accordance with the establishment requirements will not be subject to an AML/CFT enforcement action or to a significant AML/CFT supervisory action related to specified statutory/regulatory requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, nothing restricts enforcement or significant supervisory action with respect to any failure to establish the program as required. Criminal enforcement under the BSA remains unaffected.

rubrics_metrics.name: FinCEN consultation and notice requirement before enforcement/supervisory action
rubrics_metrics.description: Before initiating an AML/CFT enforcement action or a significant AML/CFT supervisory action, the agency will provide the FinCEN Director an opportunity to review and consider any input. To provide that opportunity, the agency will send written notice to the FinCEN Director of its intent to take the action at least 30 days before taking the action (unless a shorter period is necessary in the agency's sole discretion), accompanied by relevant AML/CFT information underlying the proposed action (draft report/enforcement action portions, examination workpapers, and AML/CFT information submitted by the institution, excluding privileged material). The agency will respond, to the extent reasonably practicable, to requests for additional information from the FinCEN Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This sets procedural timelines and the content of submissions to FinCEN; the 30‑day period can be shortened if necessary to remedy, prevent, or respond to unsafe or unsound practices or conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of supervisory information to FinCEN (Option 1 and Option 2) and privilege preservation
rubrics_metrics.description: Option 1: Notwithstanding FOIA/regulations, the agency permits an institution, on behalf of the agency, to disclose to the FinCEN Director, and permits the FinCEN Director to use, any information relating to an existing or potential AML/CFT enforcement or significant supervisory action to which the institution has access. Option 2: Same permission but only upon the contemporaneous disclosure of such information to the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Either option states that disclosure to FinCEN does not waive, invalidate, destroy, or otherwise affect any privilege or protection under Federal or State law (attorney‑client privilege, work‑product doctrine, bank‑examination privilege, or other confidentiality/evidentiary privileges). Disclosures are made on behalf of the agency pursuant to statutory authorization (e.g., 12 U.S.C. 1821(t)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Severability
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions of the subpart are separate and severable. If any provision is held invalid, such invalidity shall not affect other provisions or applications that can be given effect without the invalid provision or application.
